rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source-verification maintainer block on any student-facing file with practitioner citations.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Structurally, the `<!-- backing -->` block's Claims/Sources/Frameworks/Stance/OODA sections correctly function as this file's source-verification ledger (AE101's adopted convention). But this rule's own sub-clause (printed verbatim in-brief as the guidance immediately following the lead) requires DUE = publication+6mo and explicitly bans checked+6mo arithmetic ('Never checked+6mo'). Independently re-verified this session via WebFetch (not carried forward from any prior instance): klaassen-definitive-guide published 2026-02-09 (byline Klaassen confirmed) — stamp reads `checked:2026-08-23 result:OK due:2027-02-23`; correct due = 2026-08-09, already 19 days past as of today (2026-08-28), and was already 14 days past on the stamp's own checked date. klaassen-expanded-loop published 2026-05-29 (metadata `published_at: 2026-05-29T05:00:00-04:00`) — stamp reads `checked:2026-07-31 due:2027-01-31`; correct due = 2026-11-29, two months earlier than stated (not yet stale, but wrongly computed). klaassen-compound-run published 2025-12-11 (metadata `published_at: 2025-12-11T11:00:00-05:00`) — stamp reads `checked:2026-07-30 due:2027-01-30`; correct due = 2026-06-11, already 49 days past on its own checked date and 78 days past as of today. All three `due` values equal `checked + exactly 6 months` (not publication + 6 months) — a systematic arithmetic error, not a one-off typo, across every dated non-attested source in this file. Harm this rule exists to prevent: the mechanical audit (`source-freshness.sh`) trusts `due:` fields to flag re-check debt; with this arithmetic, two of the three citations are silently past due for re-verification while reading as `result:OK` with a due date five-plus months out. All three URLs sampled alive (3/3) and byline-confirmed live this session — only the due-date computation is wrong, not the cited content or the URLs.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recompute all three `due` fields from each source's actual publication date (2026-02-09 / 2026-05-29 / 2025-12-11) per §11a's formula, not from `checked`. If klaassen-definitive-guide's citation is meant to be durable/definitional rather than a currency claim, first check whether it satisfies §2a's 'specific completed event' condition (a stated philosophy/definition arguably does not, since §2a explicitly excludes an 'opinion') before reaching for due:none.

(2) check_prompts §17 — compound-and-close-1's fence has 4-5 named sub-steps with neither a No-preamble suppressor nor a skim-past body primer; low practical harm since the payload is a short end-of-turn summary, not a top-loaded plan. (3) check_prompts §40 (40b sub-guidance) — compound-and-close-1's 'the orientation and introspection' / 'the TDD bug fix' glosses are curriculum-coined labels that never appear verbatim in the earlier sibling exercises' actual prompt fences (checked orient-and-introspect.md and fix-tests-first.md directly); mitigated by the enclosing 'review this session end-to-end' instruction being fully self-sufficient on its own. (4) check_prompts §43 — the heavy session-review prompt has a reactive Esc-interrupt recovery callout in body (matching check_pedagogy §48) but no paired in-fence proactive progress-streaming instruction, which §43 explicitly wants paired with it. (5) check_pedagogy §37's own cross-reference text still reads 'auto-load = 4 surfaces' pointing at check_platform_and_boundaries §6d, which is now SIX — a compendium-internal drift, not a defect in this file's own (accurate, count-free) claim.
